title: Biochar-Assisted Agriculture: From Healthy Soil to Healthy Plants
content: Land application of biochar appears the most promising tool for managing soil and plant health in agriculture for food production. Biochar induces plant resistance, root growth and deactivated fungitoxic compounds, and supports better habituating of beneficial microorganisms as well as altering soil properties that facilitating moisture and nutrient availability. This review digest lessons from the authors’ experiences with biochar application in agriculture in addition to previous literatures to elucidate the role of biochar as "black gold" in crop production from soil health to plant health (root growth, disease control and yield and quality, ultimately linked to food health. This review provides bottom-up evidences to develop biochar-assisted agriculture in the context of ONE Health of soil-plant-food, contributing to achieving the UNSDG goals.
